queries.Context: To test whether optical near-in: autonomous near-infrared optical insect sensors measuring wing-beat frequency and body-to-wing ratio to estimate insect species richness in agricultural fields compared with Malaise traps and sweep nets
queries.Context: To acquire raw optical signals: autonomous near-infrared optical insect sensors using 810 and 970 nm LED backscatter photodiode time signals to measure wingbeat frequency and body-to-wing ratio for estimating insect species richness and biodiversity in agricultural fields
queries.Context: To convert optical backscatter: Methods for extracting wing-beat frequency and body-to-wing ratio from optical backscatter signals of insects using near-infrared sensors for biodiversity estimation
queries.Context: To derive an automated proxy fo: DBSCAN clustering of optical near-infrared insect sensor signals using wing-beat frequency and body-to-wing ratio to estimate species richness as an automated biodiversity proxy in agricultural field insect monitoring
queries.Context: To establish reference biodiver: Conventional insect sampling using Malaise traps and sweep nets in agricultural fields, specimen identification to species or morphospecies, voucher specimens, and calculation of species richness, Shannon, and Simpson biodiversity indices for reference biodiversity estimates.
queries.Context: To determine whether optical se: Spearman rank correlation between DBSCAN clustering of optical near-infrared insect sensor data and conventional species richness and diversity indices from Malaise traps and sweep nets in agricultural fields
queries.Context: To capture crop-type and season: Monitoring insect communities across agricultural crop types and seasonal sampling in central Kansas using near-infrared sensors and conventional traps to assess biodiversity variation in corn, sorghum, soybean, alfalfa, pasture, and cover crops during June and July 2020.
queries.Context: To collect continuous optical d: autonomous near-infrared insect sensor deployed 50 meters from agricultural field margin for continuous three-day monitoring in June and July to estimate invertebrate richness alongside Malaise traps and sweep nets in Kansas crops
queries.Context: To collect reference flying ins: Malaise trap sampling of flying insects in agricultural fields, single bi-directional Townes-style traps deployed for 24-hour periods near field margins to collect reference specimens for biodiversity assessment
queries.Context: To collect reference insects fr: sweep net sampling at 50, 100, and 150 m from field edges along linear transects in agricultural fields, with 50 perpendicular sweeps per location to collect reference insects for biodiversity assessment
queries.Context: To remove non-insect or unusabl: Neural network separation of insect signals from noise in near-infrared optical sensor recordings and filtering observations with clear wingbeat frequency and body-to-wing ratio features
queries.Context: To optimize the optical cluster: Optimizing DBSCAN epsilon and min_samples for clustering optical near-infrared insect sensor features wing-beat frequency and body-to-wing ratio to maximize Spearman correlation with conventional insect biodiversity metrics from Malaise traps and sweep nets
queries.Context: To evaluate optical sensor perf: Fitting separate statistical models for insect species richness and Shannon and Simpson diversity indices from Malaise traps and sweep nets, plus a combined conventional sampling model, to evaluate optical near-infrared sensor DBSCAN cluster counts as biodiversity indicators in agricultural fields.
queries.Context: To assess how sampling month, c: ANOVA Tukey HSD post hoc analyses of insect richness estimates by sampling month, crop type, field in agricultural near-infrared sensor biodiversity monitoring
